subject: Renewal + midterm capacity: proposed split and discount stack
messages:
From: Mara Lewis <mara@stratacon.ai>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: StrataCon Finance <finance@stratacon.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + midterm top-up — need invoice phasing and discount guidance

Diego,

Thanks for the catch-up last week. We're moving toward a partial top-up ahead of our June launch (roughly +40% committed capacity) and want to align it with our annual renewal in October. Two asks from our side: a) can you map how the pro-rated invoice would look if we split the top-up across two invoices, and b) what discount path you can extend for committed growth now vs. at renewal? Finance asked for concrete numbers by Friday so we can include them in the Q2 forecast.

High level constraints: 1) StrataCon prefers not to take a long-term uplift in October unless there's demonstrable unit-cost savings; 2) we need a way to keep excess token credits from the top-up available through October (no burn requirement).

Can you send options (simple A/B/C) we can present to procurement?

— Mara
Head of Platform & Data, StrataCon

Attachments: launch_plan_q2.pdf (referenced)
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Mara Lewis <mara@stratacon.ai>
Cc: StrataCon Finance <finance@stratacon.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + midterm top-up — need invoice phasing and discount guidance

Mara — thanks, and congrats again on the launch planning. Short version: we can support a split-invoice approach and offer a conditional uplift discount if you commit to a staged annual top-up. Attached is a worked example (invoice_split_example.xlsx) and three clean options below.

Option A — Short-term top-up, no annual commit
- +40% capacity billed immediately, standard midterm pricing (no uplift discount).
- Credits available in full until Oct 31; unused credits expire after that.
- Good if you need speed and minimal contractual change.

Option B — Split billing with temporary voucher and renewal anchor (recommended)
- Split the +40%: 60% billed now, 40% billed at renewal (Oct).
- Apply a 12% uplift discount on the incremental capacity if StrataCon signs a 12-month anchor at renewal for the combined committed units.
- Temporarily unlock a voucher pool (non-expiring until Oct 31) for the 40% reserved bucket.

Option C — Immediate annualize with stepped discount
- Convert +40% into an annualized commit immediately (adds to current annual baseline).
- Stepped discount: 6% now, growing to 12% on 12-month renewal; invoiced monthly.
- Best unit cost but requires procurement approval for longer-term commit.

I'm looping Karthik for pricing confirmation and Naomi for renewal incentives. If you want, we can also include a short SLA credit if uptime is mission-critical for the June launch.

Next steps: tell me which option you want to present; we'll create a short amendment + invoice mock and route to legal/finance.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: invoice_split_example.xlsx
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal + midterm top-up — need invoice phasing and discount guidance

Diego — quick pricing notes inline. Pasting my comments rather than a separate doc so Diego has the thread: 

> Option A — Short-term top-up, no annual commit
- Pricing: keep list price, offer a one-off onboarding credit of 3% of the top-up value to offset migration/ops during launch.

> Option B — Split billing with temporary voucher and renewal anchor (recommended)
- Pricing: 12% uplift discount on incremental units is fine if commit >= 12 months and overall ARR delta > $150k. Otherwise we can tier to 8% for a 6-month anchor.
- Voucher: make the voucher non-expiring until Oct 31 as Diego suggested, but voucher cannot be used for cross-account transfers.

> Option C — Immediate annualize with stepped discount
- Pricing: floor discount 8% on immediate annualization, scales to 12% if they add a 2-year visibility clause (we'd reserve right to review in year 2).

Ops asks: Naomi — confirm whether Finance will accept split-invoice treatment (charge now + charge at renewal) but show credits on a single renewal amendment. If yes, we can send an invoice mock with proration lines.

Jordan — can you flag if the SLA credit for launch is an escalation-level ask? We should keep margin for a small uptime rebate (0.25% ARR) rather than big service credits.

-Karthik
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Mara Lewis <mara@stratacon.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, StrataCon Finance <finance@stratacon.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + midterm top-up — need invoice phasing and discount guidance

Mara — thanks for the patience. Based on internal alignment here are three polished options you can present to procurement (I've included the finance-friendly language you requested). We can have a formal amendment + invoice mock ready within 48 hours once you pick an option.

1) Speed-first (Option A, fast) — no long-term change
- Immediate +40% billed in May. One-off onboarding credit = 3% of the top-up invoice value applied against the May invoice.
- Credits usable through Oct 31. Remaining balance expires Nov 1.
- Pros: fastest; Cons: higher unit cost at renewal.

2) Balanced (Option B, recommended) — split + renewal anchor
- 60% billed now (May), 40% reserved and invoiced on Oct 1 (applies to renewal amendment).
- If StrataCon signs a 12-month renewal amendment on Oct 1 for the combined baseline, Redwood will apply a 12% discount on the incremental units added by the top-up (applies from Oct 1 onward).
- Voucher: 40% reserved bucket will be converted into a voucher visible in the Console; available until Oct 31 and applied to usage before being invoiced.
- Finance-friendly phrasing: split invoicing will appear as two line items; the Oct line will include a conditional credit that only triggers on signed amendment. We provide an invoice mock showing proration lines (attached).

3) Efficiency-first (Option C, unit-cost optimized) — immediate annualize
- Add +40% to the committed baseline immediately and bill monthly across remaining term; discount floor 8% (scales to 12% with a 24-month visibility clause).
- Requires PO/commit sign-off from procurement.

Additional notes:
- SLA rebate: we're offering a minor launch SLA rebate (0.25% ARR) in Options B/C if uptime drops below agreed thresholds during the 60-day launch window.
- Legal: amendment language will include an explicit voucher expiry clause for Option A and B (we can soften to Oct 31 per your ask).

Please let me know which option your team wants to present. If helpful, I'll schedule a 30-minute procurement + finance walkthrough with Naomi and Karthik to go line-by-line on the invoice mock.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOW_v3.pdf, invoice_split_example.xlsx
